3. This Witness Statement addresses Questions 8, 9(a) and 9(d) of the 4 February Letter. Other Questions which are within the FSD’s purview will be addressed in the witness statements of other relevant officers of the FSD to the Committee.

4. The following paragraphs set out the decisions made by me as the Incident Commander after the fire was upgraded to No. 3 Alarm in answer to **Questions 8, 9(a) and 9(d)**. The response should be read together with the timeline and account of the No. 3 Alarm Fire provided in paragraphs 18 to 29 of the Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah.

[Questions 8 and 9(a)]

5. As stated in paragraph 19 of the Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah, I was the first of the two Incident Commanders of the No. 3 Alarm Fire (from 1502 hours to 1533 hours). At 1504 hours on 26 November 2025, I received a telephone call from the Fire Services Communications Centre (“**FSCC**”), which instructed me to attend a No.3 Alarm Fire at Wang Cheong House, Wang Fuk Court.

6. Upon my arrival at scene at 1519 hours, I took on the role of Incident Commander. I put on my personal protective equipment and proceeded to Wang Cheong House. I observed that north-west façade of Wang Cheong House and east façade Wang Tai House were well alight and that the fire had already spread to Wang Shing House with its south-west façade (portion of middle to upper floors) also alight. Burning bamboo sticks and debris kept falling from height from Wang Cheong House.
